items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: I went with Willy Bryant and Battles was in that band with Willy Bryant.

ctx.x: oh my goodness, here I am going to build my whole career, I says if I miss that, the rest of the band is going to say where the hell did you get that drummer from, you know. But I did it and I knew how to follow the conductor. Of course the other drummer in the pit played the tympani and vibes. So, I went to rehearsal frightened to death, now, I never did this before, in the pit, had a big band, had about 18 or 20 fiddles from the New York Philharmonic, bassoons, bass horns and everything, all sitting in the pit…

and we rehearsed about two weeks, then we took the show on to Philadelphia and New Haven and Boston. Altogether about three weeks out on the road before we came into New York. Well by then I knew the score backwards. Everybody did. You know, everybody. You knew the score backwards. When you hit New York, you could play with your eyes closed, because I was so used to playing shows with Cab, Benny Carter, Willy Bryant, whereas the average Broadway show is two hours long, isn't it, you would say?
